source_refs.note: Topic 12.5.2 with Figures 12.4 and 12.5, printed pages 277-278.

blocks.text: NOx takes part in a series of reactions leading to ozone, aldehydes, peroxyacyl nitrates (PANs) and peroxybenzoyl nitrate (PBN). PAN is one member of the peroxyacyl nitrates, general structure RC(O)OONO2 (Figure 12.4); in peroxyacetyl nitrate R is CH3, but other hydrocarbon chains may be present. The formation of PAN (Figure 12.5): the main component of oxidising smog is ozone, which oxidises a hydrocarbon to an aldehyde; the aldehyde reacts with a hydroxyl radical to give an acyl radical; the acyl radical reacts with oxygen to give a peroxyacyl radical, which finally reacts with nitrogen dioxide to form peroxyacyl nitrate.

blocks.alt: Structure: R bonded to a C that carries a double-bonded O above it; the C is bonded to O, which is bonded to a second O, which is bonded to N. The N carries a + charge, a double-bonded O to the right and a single-bonded O with a minus charge below.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.4: General structure of PANs (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.4).

blocks.alt: A cycle drawn as an ellipse with clockwise arrows. Reactive Hydrocarbon (green box) reacts with O3 to give RCH2• at the top of the cycle; with O2 this gives RCH2O2•; with NO it gives RCH2O• + NO2; with O2 it gives HO2 + RCHO at the bottom; HO2 with NO gives NO2 + HO• on the left; HO• with RCH3 gives RCH2• again. From RCHO a vertical chain: with OH• to RC•=O, with O2 to RC(=O)OO•, with NO2 to RC(=O)OONO2.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.5: Mechanism of PAN formation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.5).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 12.5 has three slips: RCH2O. for RCH2O2., OONO3 for OONO2 in the PAN formula, and reversed arrows on the left half of the cycle. They are drawn correctly above.
What does PAN stand for, give its general formula, and name the compounds responsible for its formation.
